items.text: Selves taking 80% or more of their prescribed pills hold a five-year mortality of 15.0% against 24.6% among selves taking less, with a lipid-lowering drug, and 15.1% against 28.3% with an inert pill. Among 1,255 selves taking an inert pill in one heart trial, 98 of them, 7.8%, take less than 75% of it, and an all-cause mortality hazard ratio of 0.52 stands with the higher taking, 95% confidence interval 0.38 to 0.71; among 2,092 selves taking an inert pill in a second, 141 of them, 6.7%, take less than 75%, mortality comes at 14.8%, and the hazard ratio is 0.52, 0.35 to 0.79. Per 10% more of it taken the hazard ratios are 0.89, 0.84 to 0.95, and 0.90, 0.83 to 0.98. With the last adherence measuring dropped the hazard ratios are 0.75, 0.49 to 1.15, and 0.61, 0.38 to 0.96; with the last two dropped, 0.77, 0.49 to 1.22, and 0.54, 0.34 to 0.88. Varying the cutoff from 50% to 95%, the strongest stand at 55%, hazard ratio 0.42, 0.27 to 0.66, and at 60%, 0.42, 0.23 to 0.74. Adjusting for demographics, cardiovascular risk factors and education leaves the first trial's association alike at each outcome and attenuates the second's at non-cardiovascular mortality.
items.from: Taking an inert pill, how much of it is taken, and a five-year mortality
